headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.3516). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 13 studies yielded an effect size of 0.94 (95% CI: 0.82–1.06), indicating no statistically significant association between alcohol and bladder cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 79.09%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.

studies.Reference: Bladder cancer, tobacco smoking, coffee and alcohol drinking in Brescia, northern Italy.
studies.Population: Hospital-based cases and controls in Brescia, northern Italy
studies.comparison_type: Current alcohol drinkers versus non-drinkers, men

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A total of 172 incident cases (135 men and 37 women) and 578 controls (398 men and 180 women) were enrolled.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: A total of 172 incident cases (135 men and 37 women) and 578 controls (398 men and 180 women) were enrolled.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: A dose-response relationship was found in men, with the highest risk in the highest category of exposure: drinkers of more than 5 cups per day had an OR of 4.5 (95% CI: 1.2-16.8). The ORs for current alcohol drinkers were 2.1 (95% CI: 1.0-4.8) in men and 3.4 (95% CI: 1.2-9.7) in women; according to grams of ethanol drunk per day (grams/day, g/d) the ORs were: 1.7 (1-20 g/d), 1.6 (21-40 g/d), 4.3 (41-60 g/d) and 4.6 (61+ g/d) in men and 3.1 (1-20 g/d) and 3.9 (21+ g/d) in women.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: The ORs for current alcohol drinkers were 2.1 (95% CI: 1.0-4.8) in men and 3.4 (95% CI: 1.2-9.7) in women; according to grams of ethanol drunk per day (grams/day, g/d) the ORs were: 1.7 (1-20 g/d), 1.6 (21-40 g/d), 4.3 (41-60 g/d) and 4.6 (61+ g/d) in men and 3.1 (1-20 g/d) and 3.9 (21+ g/d) in women.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: The ORs for current alcohol drinkers were 2.1 (95% CI: 1.0-4.8) in men and 3.4 (95% CI: 1.2-9.7) in women
extraction_supporting_text.design: investigated in a hospital-based case-control study in Brescia, northern Italy
extraction_supporting_text.continent: Brescia, northern Italy
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: the consumption of coffee and alcohol and bladder cancer was investigated
